issues.description: Method signature mismatch for Milkable.messageOnMilk: The problem statement and UML specify a parameterless method messageOnMilk() returning String, and the template Main.java calls m.messageOnMilk() with no arguments. In the solution repository, Milkable declares messageOnMilk(double volume) and Goat/Seal implement messageOnMilk(double), introducing a double parameter. This discrepancy will cause compilation errors for students following the template or the problem text and creates ambiguity about the intended API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable API consistent with the problem statement and template by changing the interface to declare a parameterless method: String messageOnMilk(); then update Seal and Goat to implement messageOnMilk() and return the specified format: "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (e.g., "Seal Clarabelle is milked"). Alternatively, if the volume parameter is intended, update the problem statement, UML, and the template Main.java to require and use messageOnMilk(double volume) consistently and document the expected output format (e.g., include volume in the returned string). The preferred fix is to remove the double parameter from the solution to align with the stated tasks and examples.

issues.description: The concept of milking a Milkable animal is represented with conflicting method signatures across artifacts: the problem statement (UML and textual instructions) and the template Main.java expect a no-argument method named messageOnMilk() returning a String (and specify the return value format "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). The solution repository instead defines the Milkable interface method as messageOnMilk(double volume) and implements Goat.messageOnMilk(double) and Seal.messageOnMilk(double). This mismatch (no-arg messageOnMilk() vs messageOnMilk(double)) prevents a clear 1:1 mapping from the problem requirements to the provided API and will cause compilation/usage confusion (calls to messageOnMilk() in the template/problem examples do not match the solution's signature).
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the Milkable API across all artifacts. Preferred fix (to match the problem statement and template usage): change the solution to declare Milkable.messageOnMilk() with no parameters returning String, and update Goat and Seal to implement public String messageOnMilk() returning the specified format (e.g., "Goat Buttinsky is milked"). Alternatively (less preferred), update the problem statement and template to require messageOnMilk(double volume) and ensure all example usages and tests call the method with a volume parameter.
